classification.difficultyReason: Identify a right-angled triangular end and then use its sloping edge as a side of the rectangular ramp face, retaining an exact intermediate value.

content.prompt: The diagram shows part of a skate board ramp. (It is a prism whose cross-section is a right-angled triangle.) Use the information in the diagram to find:

spec.description: Unshaded triangular prism with solid visible edges and dashed hidden edges AE, ED and EF. Ordinary source blue/red strokes use black; dashes retain hidden-edge meaning.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding right-triangular ends ADE and BCF; DC=5 m, CF=4 m, BF=2.5 m. ABCD is the sloping rectangular face.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels and dimensions visible; neither requested length supplied.

sizing.exceptionReason: Six required vertex labels and three external dimensions need more width than a simple triangle.

answer.short:
$\frac{3\sqrt{21}}{2}\text{ m}$

Use $BC^2=\frac{89}{4}$ and $AB=5\text{ m}$ on the rectangular ramp face.
answer.worked:
The sloping face $ABCD$ is a rectangle, so $AB=DC=5\text{ m}$ and triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$.
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=AB^2+BC^2\\AC^2&=5^2+\frac{89}{4}\\AC^2&=\frac{189}{4}\\AC&=\frac{3\sqrt{21}}{2}\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
